Cc: audit_lead@catalyst-audit.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG / CAIQ evidence packaging — a couple of clarifying asks

Hi Irene / Grace,

Thanks again for the intake packet you shared last week. Catalyst is starting their SIG/CAIQ review and we have two quick questions before we lock in the sample window:

1) Evidence packaging: can you provide a single index CSV that lists artifacts we can expect (file name, control mapped, owner, last-modified, short description)? That will speed up our intake.

2) Escrow / auditor access: Northwest policy requires either an escrow snapshot or time-limited auditor access for certain encryption and key-management artifacts. Do you have a standard approach (escrow vs time-limited read-only access to S3/Drive) you prefer for FedRAMP/ISO customers?

3) Sample window length: Catalyst typically requests a 30-day extraction window plus a few historical examples. Are there retention or snapshot limitations we should know about?

We'd like to schedule a 30-minute evidence review next week after you confirm the packaging approach.

Megan
Megan O'Neill
Head of Vendor Risk, Northwind Financial

+1 415-555-0198

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SIG / CAIQ evidence packaging — a couple of clarifying asks

Hi Megan — great questions. Looping in Priya (controls/evidence owner) and Karthik (platform infra) so we can answer both packaging and technical constraints. Below is our proposed approach and a short list of decisions we need from you.

Proposed approach (short):
- Artifact index: we can produce a single CSV with columns: filename, control_id (SIG/CAIQ mapping), artifact_owner, last_modified, retention_policy, and short description. We'll attach an index stub to this thread.
- Packaging: we prefer to stage evidence in a time-bound read-only S3 location and share pre-signed links for auditors. For certain cryptographic key documents (KMS change logs, key rotation proofs) some customers prefer escrow copies; we can support either.
- Sample window: standard is 30 days for snapshots plus up to three point-in-time examples (e.g., prior rotations). Snapshots are generated from snapshot-extraction pipeline; they do not include private keys.

Decisions needed from Northwind before we start:
1) Escrow vs pre-signed link — which does your audit team require?
2) Do you require a notarized attestation for key rotation events?

Action owners / next steps:
- Priya: will assemble the artifact index and package examples (ETA: 48 hours).
- Karthik: will confirm technical constraints on pre-signed links, snapshot TTL, and sample extraction artifacts (ETA: EOD today).
- Irene (me): schedule evidence review once Priya confirms index.

Attachment: redwood_artifact_index_stub.csv (small)

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick note on packaging and timelines.

- Artifact index: attached is a preliminary index extract (redwood_artifact_index.csv). It includes the most commonly requested artifacts: SOC reports, config snapshots, IAM role lists, KMS rotation logs (summary), and backup snapshots references. I'll continue to enrich it with mapping to SIG/CAIQ controls.
- Evidence packaging: for auditor convenience we stage artifacts in a dedicated S3 bucket with folder structure by control family, then generate pre-signed links per-folder. If Northwind requires escrow, we can produce a ZIP package with MD5/SHA256 checksums and deliver via secure transfer.
- Retention notes: our standard operational retention for logs is 180 days; backups and snapshots are retained per customer SLA (can be extended on request).

Attachments: redwood_artifact_index.csv (full index), snapshot_extraction_notes.txt

I'll target sending the final, SIG-mapped index by Friday morning.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Megan O'Neill <megan@northwind.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 16:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG / CAIQ evidence packaging — a couple of clarifying asks

Megan / Priya / Irene — quick technical clarifications from infra: 

1) Pre-signed links vs escrow: pre-signed S3 links are simplest operationally and we can set TTLs per link (48–168 hours). For regulatory requirements where a custodial snapshot is mandatory we can create an escrow package that excludes private key material and provide tamper-evident checksums.

2) KMS and key rotation artifacts: we can export key rotation metadata and HSM audit statements (where available). We do not export secret key material. See attached summary (kms_key_rotation_summary.pdf).

3) Snapshot extraction: our extraction tool can provide point-in-time filesystem/config dumps and database logical exports (redacted). For FedRAMP-specific asks, we recommend 3 point-in-time samples within the last 12 months plus the 30-day window.

Constraints:
- We cannot provide live console credentials to external auditors; access is via read-only exports or time-limited links.
- For very large exports (DB dumps >50GB) we may need a staged transfer and extra lead time (2–3 business days).

If these details work, Priya/Irene — we can trigger extraction tomorrow.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
